items.title: Pharmaceutical advertising and drug recommendations by consumer-facing artificial intelligence: a controlled study
items.rationale: Controlled study shows injected pharma ads steer consumer LLM drug picks while guideline concordance stays high — a patient-safety risk that evades accuracy checks.
items.excerpt: Controlled study: injecting pharmaceutical advertising shifted LLM treatment selection toward the promoted drug while guideline concordance stayed high, so the shifts could evade correctness checks; the advertising influence was often undisclosed. (Published date via Crossref; article page blocked.)

items.title: MDCalc launches a 'rumble strip' for doctors using generative AI tools
items.rationale: New clinician-facing product launch (CrossCover) that cross-checks medical chatbot answers at the point of care.
items.excerpt: MDCalc, a medical reference tool site, is launching CrossCover, a tool meant to help clinicians trust the answers of medical AI chatbots.

items.title: AI triage algorithms yield varied results in real-world use
items.rationale: RSNA 2026 preview: system-wide UW deployment across 742,000+ exams — big turnaround gains for some findings, none for PE and ICH; sobering real-world evidence.
items.excerpt: RSNA 2026 preview: University of Washington evaluated staged system-wide deployment of multiple AI triage tools across 742,000+ imaging exams. Turnaround fell 76% for endotracheal tube malposition, 53% for rib fracture and 29% for vessel occlusion, but PE and intracranial hemorrhage saw no improvement.

items.title: Synthetic data to lower barriers towards equitable artificial intelligence in rapid diagnostic test interpretation
items.rationale: SynSight reads HIV and COVID-19 rapid tests at 98-99% accuracy using a model trained on synthetic images — cheaper path to AI diagnostics in low-resource settings.
items.excerpt: Rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) support affordable disease diagnosis. Machine learning (ML) can improve RDT interpretation but often relies on large, proprietary, and costly real-world image libraries. We present SynSight – a ML-enabled RDT segmentation and classification pipeline trained on synthetic data.
